steps.body: Integers, fractions, decimals, negatives — they all live on **one number line**, so they can all be ordered together. The trick is to picture each one's spot: negatives left of zero, positives right, and fractions/decimals in the gaps between whole numbers. Then read left to right, smallest to largest.
Put both forms on one fraction line.

widget.prompt: On a line divided into fourths, 0.5 is 2/4. Place the marker at the greater value: 3/4.

commonPlacements.feedback: The second mark is 2/4 = 1/2 = 0.5. Move one fourth to the right to reach 3/4.

widget.successFeedback: 3/4 lies to the right of 2/4, which is 0.5. Different written forms can name points on the same number line.
widget.lowFeedback: This point is below both 0.5 and 3/4. Translate 0.5 to 2/4, then move right one fourth.
widget.highFeedback: This point is greater than 3/4. Stop at the third of the four equal marks.

hints: Put both in the same form.

predict.prompt: A fraction and a decimal — are they even the same KIND of number, comparable at all?
predict.reveal: Both are costumes for the same rational numbers — rewrite either one and they stand on a single number line together. Form never blocks comparison.

explanationVariants: -1/2 = -0.5 and -3/4 = -0.75; -0.5 is farther right, so -1/2 is greater.

widget.ltFeedback: -3/4 = -0.75 is farther from zero, making it SMALLER. -1/2 = -0.5 is greater.
widget.eqFeedback: -0.5 and -0.75 are different points. -1/2 (-0.5) is greater.
widget.successFeedback: Right — -1/2 = -0.5 sits right of -3/4 = -0.75, so -1/2 is greater.

steps.body: A reliable method: **convert everything to the same form** — usually decimals — then order. −2, −1/2, 0.75, 1.5 become −2, −0.5, 0.75, 1.5. Now the order is obvious: most-negative first. Watch the classic trap — among negatives, −2 is SMALLER than −1/2, even though 2 looks bigger than 1/2.

explanationVariants: -2 = -2.0 is farther left than -1/2 = -0.5, so -2 is SMALLER.
The bigger-looking negative (-2) is actually the smaller value.

widget.eqFeedback: -2 and -0.5 are far apart on the line. -2 is much smaller.
widget.gtFeedback: -1/2 = -0.5 is closer to zero, making it GREATER, not smaller. -2 is the smaller value.
widget.successFeedback: Right — -2 is farther left than -1/2 (-0.5), so -2 is the smaller value, even though 2 > 1/2 in size.

hints: Where does each sit on the line?
-2 is two full steps left; -1/2 is only half a step left.

steps.body: Locate the leftmost value in a mixed set.

predict.prompt: 0.75, -2, 1.5, -1/2 — a decimal, a negative integer, another decimal and a negative fraction. What decides the order?

options.label: Position on the number line — the written form does not matter
Group them by form first: integers, then decimals, then fractions
Compare the digits: 2 beats 1.5 beats 0.75 beats 1/2

predict.reveal: Position, and nothing else. A number's form is just how it is written down; -1/2 and -0.5 are the same point. Put each one where it falls on the line and the order reads off left to right.

widget.prompt: Among 0.75, -2, 1.5, and -1/2, place the marker at the smallest value—the point farthest left.

commonPlacements.feedback: -0.5 is -1/2. It lies left of the positive values but still right of -2.
0.75 is positive, so both negative values lie to its left.
1.5 is the greatest value in this set, not the smallest.

widget.successFeedback: -2 is farthest left. Continuing right gives -1/2, 0.75, and 1.5, regardless of how each number is written.
widget.lowFeedback: This point is smaller than every stated value. Choose one of the four values in the set.
widget.highFeedback: The smallest stated value is farther left. Convert -1/2 to -0.5 if that helps compare positions.

explanationVariants: 2/5 = 0.4, which is less than 0.6, so 0.6 is greater.

widget.prompt: Use 0.5 as a benchmark. Which is greater: 2/5 or 0.6?
widget.eqFeedback: 2/5 = 0.4, not 0.6. They're different, and 0.6 is greater.
widget.gtFeedback: 2/5 = 0.4, smaller than 0.6. Converting the fraction to a decimal makes the comparison clear: 0.6 > 0.4.
widget.successFeedback: Right — 2/5 = 0.4, which is less than 0.6, so 0.6 is greater.

steps.body: The whole number system on one line.
hints: Convert each to a decimal first: -1.5, 0.25, -3, 0, 2.
explanationVariants: As decimals: -3, -1.5, 0, 0.25, 2. Smallest first: -3, then -1.5, then 0, then 1/4, then 2.
-3 is farthest left, 2 farthest right; 0 sits in the middle with 1/4 just to its right.

misorderFeedback.feedback: -1.5 isn't smaller than -3 — -3 is farther left. -3 comes first.
1/4 = 0.25 is greater than 0, so 0 comes before 1/4, not after.

widget.missFeedback: Convert all to decimals: -3, -1.5, 0, 0.25, 2. Order them left to right on the line, smallest (most negative) first.
widget.successFeedback: Ordered — the full number system on one line: -3, -1.5, 0, 1/4, 2.

takeaways: Integers, fractions, decimals, and negatives all share one number line.
Convert to a common form (usually decimals), then order left to right.
Among negatives, the bigger-looking number is the smaller value.
steps.teaser: Course complete — you've built the whole number system, positive and negative.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Same form, then order.** To compare 1/2 and 0.7, make both decimals: 1/2 = 0.5, so 0.7 > 0.5. Converting everything to decimals turns any mixed comparison into an easy one.

explanationVariants: 1/2 = 0.5, which is less than 0.7, so 0.7 is greater.

options.feedback: Right — 1/2 = 0.5, which is less than 0.7, so 0.7 is greater.

options.label: Equal
options.feedback: 1/2 = 0.5, not 0.7. They differ, and 0.7 is greater.
